PullRequest.Title: agentHost: fix scoped debug log export
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

- group client-owned AHP wire logs by a stable logical-host ID while preserving the actual protocol connection ID in each JSONL entry
- include reconnect-created, rotated, and older output-channel log segments without mixing overlapping connections
- stream browser-owned files without a silent inline byte budget and fail explicitly when desktop archive inputs cannot be saved
- surface unexpected enumeration and read failures while retaining expected missing-log behavior

## Validation

- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/common/ahpJsonlLogger.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/common/relayTransport.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/browser/agentHostIpcChannelTransport.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/exportAgentHostDebugLogs.test.ts` (47 passing)
- `npm run typecheck-client`
- ESLint on all changed TypeScript files
- `git diff --check`

(Written by Copilot)

Scenarios.Scenario: Agent Host protocol logging during initial connection and relay/WebSocket reconnects
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Connection establishment must complete before protocol traffic proceeds. The changed logical-host hashing happens synchronously only when each logger is constructed; existing JSON serialization and file appends remain off the connection handshake after construction and are queued by the logger.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Establish WebSocket, tunnel, SSH, WSL, dev-container, or cloud-sandbox transport
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One establishment per initial connection or reconnect attempt; unchanged by the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same transport establishment occurred; relay loggers used the seed ID rather than the newly established connection ID.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The establishment is on the connection critical path, but the diff only passes the established connection ID into logger construction.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create the AHP log directory and append coalesced JSONL batches
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One memoized directory creation per logger and sequential writes capped at 1 MiB per batch; unchanged. Rotation remains capped at five segments per logger.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same queued directory creation, file-size stat, batched append, and rotation occurred.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Queued logging I/O is not awaited by protocol send/receive and therefore is off the message critical path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of established/re-established transport connections and logged protocol bytes. The diff adds one SHA-1 computation per logger construction, not per message.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One logger is created per established transport. Relay reconnect attempts are serialized by ReconnectingTransport; each logger retains the existing promise-queue serialization and 1 MiB write coalescing.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Directory creation remains memoized per logger; no shared cache is added or defeated. Rotation and batch state are unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: logger construction and queued write ownership are directly visible in the changed factories and AhpJsonlLogger.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Reconnect frequency varies, but the added CPU work is constant per established connection and tiny relative to network establishment.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The changed connection identity does not increase boundary cardinality or move file I/O onto the handshake/message critical path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Opening the Agent Debug AHP wire-log view, including while wire logging is disabled
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The view waits for source enumeration before rendering a selected historical log. The diff makes one AHP-directory metadata resolve occur even when logging is currently disabled so historical files remain visible.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve the current log session's ahp directory with child metadata
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One directory resolve per wire-log view show; filenames are filtered in memory. Before the diff this was zero when the logging setting was disabled and one when enabled.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: When logging was disabled, enumeration skipped the directory entirely and could not expose historical logs; enabled enumeration already resolved the same directory.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The metadata resolve delays initial source rendering, but occurs only when this diagnostic view is explicitly opened.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of files in the current log session's ahp directory. Log sessions are externally retained in a bounded history, while reconnect-created files can increase current-directory cardinality.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: A single enumeration runs per view show; source filtering and sorting are synchronous after one directory resolve. Live refresh rereads the selected file but does not re-enumerate sources.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No application cache; warm behavior depends on filesystem/provider metadata caching. No repeated enumeration occurs during live file watching.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the removed configuration guard and sole caller's show/load flow are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Current-session reconnect counts can vary, but this is a user-opened diagnostics surface and performs metadata-only work once per show.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. The added single metadata enumeration is necessary to expose historical logs and is not a realistic latency regression on this non-hot diagnostic path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Export Agent Host debug logs to a native ZIP or browser-selected folder
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Collection and destination selection start concurrently. Collection awaits the existing host collectDebugLogs RPC and local metadata enumeration; after destination selection, save streams/copies each selected client file and the host artifact before completion.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Request host-owned debug-log artifact and read remote artifact chunks
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One collectDebugLogs request, then artifact bytes in at most 1 MiB sequential chunks; unchanged by the client-file collection changes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same host collection and bounded chunk protocol were used.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Host artifact production and later transfer are on export completion's critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Enumerate renderer/shared rotated logs, output-channel folders, AHP logs, and sidecars
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two process-log directory resolves, one AHP-directory resolve, up to two sidecar stats, and one resolve per output_* folder. The diff changes output-channel matching from the newest match per requested filename to all matching historical folders.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The prior search stopped after finding one newest file for each requested channel; rotated process/AHP enumeration already scanned their directories.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Metadata enumeration is on collection's critical path, though collection runs concurrently with destination selection.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Stream each URI-backed client log to a browser destination or into the native ZIP
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One sequential stream per selected client log; bytes scale with all selected historical logs. Native ZIP entry count is capped at 1000. Browser export has no aggregate byte cap but uses backpressured streams.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: File/vscodeUserData resources were already streamed. Other schemes were eagerly read and converted to retained inline strings under a shared 30 MiB cap, silently omitting additional bytes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All selected bytes must be read and written before export completes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: No subprocess is started by the changed export path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Total bytes and file count across process rotations, matching output-channel histories, AHP reconnect/rotation logs, sidecars, and host artifact entries. Effective cardinality is one stream per selected file rather than per log record.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Destination selection and collection run in parallel. Collection directory scans and per-file metadata operations are sequential. Browser folder export streams files sequentially; native export makes one createZipFile IPC whose implementation streams local files, while remote host artifacts are downloaded in sequential 1 MiB chunks.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No export-result cache or coalescing; each explicit export re-enumerates and rereads current files. Warm behavior is limited to OS/provider caches. Negative sidecar and missing AHP-directory results are not retained between separate exports.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: all collection loops, provider boundaries, native ZIP implementation, and browser streaming consumer were traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Long-lived windows and reconnect-heavy hosts can produce larger complete exports, but the operation is explicit, sequential, streaming, and intended to include those histories; exact disk/network duration depends on log volume.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. Historical inclusion increases intentional export I/O, but avoids the prior eager 30 MiB buffer/string retention and remains sequential/backpressured. The expanded output-folder scan is user-triggered metadata work and not a high-confidence actionable regression.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 18 changed files. No diff-introduced performance finding met the reporting threshold. The main change converts non-local client-log collection from capped eager buffering to URI-backed streaming; a regression-fix record was attempted after blame identified 4f34cd7973989fc40b9aacd64be02263d3f1673c, but the regression-fix reporting tool failed twice.
